observations.title: Third case fixture attribution is wrong: mesh-mesh.xml, not mesh-mesh-two-assets.xml
observations.detail: S2 README lines 212/215, receipt line 325 and the delivery record line 91 attribute the mesh-mesh case to fixtures/g10-p5-mesh-multicontact/mesh-mesh-two-assets.xml. The M3 mesh-case-manifest.json records xml=fixtures/g10-p5-mesh-multicontact/mesh-mesh.xml with xml_sha256=bb9ffb2f979129bbac410e9959088528f35180d14f5572c9a52631fa2ed86d8d and qpos z=0.18. QA measurement: mesh-mesh.xml sha256 is exactly bb9ffb2f…; the M3 case bins are nmesh=2, nmeshvert=16, nmeshpoly=12 with mesh_vertnum=[8,8] and mesh_polynum=[6,6], i.e. two cubes (only mesh-mesh.xml uses cube + cube_b scaled 0.9 with qpos z=0.18). mesh-mesh-two-assets.xml (sha 1d7115…) is cube + tetra (12 verts, 10 polygons, qpos z=0.09) and is the fixture of the S3/S4 U6 branch case.
observations.proposed_action: Correct the fixture name to mesh-mesh.xml in README §8.2, in the receipt s2 description and in the delivery record bin_inputs note, and cite xml_sha256=bb9ffb2f… from the M3 manifest as provenance; align the task-card acceptance path wording through a normify fix addendum.
observations.impact: bins and S2 tests are unaffected (tests read bins only, never the XML); evidence traceability points at the wrong fixture and future slices may mix the two cases

observations.title: from_model_input only supports a single-world frame; nworld>1 has no entry
observations.detail: from_model_input requires frame lengths ngeom*3 / ngeom*9 (single world), while validate_inputs requires geom_xpos length nworld*ngeom*3. Therefore meta.nworld>1 always yields InvalidArgument through from_model_input + inputs_from_snapshot. nworld>1 was not tested in this slice, and there is no adapter entry that repeats the frame (the view fields are pub, but then the bridge validation is bypassed).
observations.proposed_action: State in the README/ledger that the S1 bridge is nworld==1 only and define the multi-world assembly for S3 (repeat the frame or add a new entry)
observations.impact: S3 wiring needs an explicit multi-world decision; no effect on S2 deliverables

observations.title: Sidecar predicate duplicated between run() and mesh_poly_sidecar_present
observations.detail: mesh_poly_sidecar_present copies run()'s inline condition !inputs.mesh_polynum.is_empty() (src/runtime/collision_gpu.rs:162). Not refactoring run is consistent with this slice's contract, but the two predicates can drift.
observations.proposed_action: In the next slice, make run() call the helper (zero behaviour change)

observations.title: README wording overstates how the bridge test's meta is derived
observations.detail: README §8.2 says the from_model_input bridge test passes validate with a meta derived from the 30 fields/frame. In the test the meta is hand-built; only ngeom and noct come from the snapshot counts, everything else is a literal (naconmax=64, efc_width=4, ...).
observations.proposed_action: Reword to 'hand-built meta (ngeom/noct taken from snapshot counts)'

observations.title: Literal regulated terms in a negative sentence in the shared evidence directory
observations.detail: docs/development-evidence/product-collision-inputs-wiring/s1-observation-closure-receipt.json:70 (S1 closure, not part of the S2 diff) contains the six regulated claim terms verbatim inside a negative sentence. Files changed by S2 itself scan 0 hits, but a directory-wide forbid_claim scan would flag it.
observations.proposed_action: Rephrase without the literal terms (for example 'no window-type, coverage-type, precision-type or equivalence-type claim')
observations.impact: possible false positive in future directory-wide checks

observations.title: The native feature path is not covered by the default gate
observations.detail: Gate clippy/unit use default features; from_model_input (cfg native-model-probe) and its ignored bridge test are outside the gate. The 3 default-feature host tests do run in unit (997 = 994 + 3, which is good). The native side is currently covered only by logs/s2-fmt-clippy.log's explicit clippy plus a manual targeted rerun.
observations.proposed_action: Register a targeted gate item for clippy/test with --features native-model-probe
observations.impact: future changes to the bridge have no automatic protection

observations.title: 'gate ran twice with identical results' has only the final run archived
observations.detail: s2-gate.log states the gate ran twice with identical results and counts, but the four json files under .normify/runs/<task>/ are overwritten in place; only the final run (final tree) is on disk. Same pattern as the S1 review observation.
observations.proposed_action: Keep both run directories, or state in the receipt that only the final tree is archived
